shots.sourceNoteText: Let's start with a couple establishing shots of space. Maybe it's, and it's going to be drifting. So maybe we start with a borrowed establishing shot of the planet, the moons, and some cosmic stuff, maybe even meteor racing by. And we're going to drift into frame, cut into the interior of the spaceship. The air will fade into, or will drift over into Harper's profile coming in and locking the stars. We're going to do something kind of dramatic here. When we get to her floating, we don't want to see her body out because we want to bounce back out to see that she's floating. I wonder if we can do this. Maybe that we get tiresome as kind of a runner where we connect all the transitions with either a speed zoom or an actual camera movement to the next cut. That would probably be hard. Consistency would probably be tough. Maybe we can do that where we can do that in a few places though. Just be tiring to try and keep it up for the whole thing. Maybe for select scenes and cuts between the scenes we can do that.
